title_en: On the Faith Against the Arians
author: Eustathius of Antioch
occasion: The surviving fragment defends the full divinity of Christ against Arian claims by interpreting Christ's saying 'I am the way and the truth and the life.' It argues that the human 'way' leads believers to the divine 'truth and life' of the Father.
argument: Eustathius begins by presenting the manhood of Christ as the starting point of the fairest paths of righteousness, leading believers to better pursuits. This human Christ fittingly joins believers to the Spirit, guides them into paradise, and restores them to their proper pasture. He then interprets Christ's saying 'I am the way and the truth and the life': the name 'way' signifies the human, bodily, visible covering, since a way is a portion of earth and a perceptible ground. The names 'truth' and 'life' signify the nature of the Father, because truth is an intelligible reality that falls under neither sight nor touch.

outline.move: The manhood of Christ is introduced as the beginning of the fairest paths of righteousness, leading believers to better pursuits.
The human Christ joins believers to the Spirit, guides them into paradise, and restores them to their proper pasture, prompting the quotation of John 14:6.
The saying is interpreted: 'way' signifies Christ's human, bodily, visible covering, while 'truth' and 'life' signify the Father's intelligible nature.

cast.name: Christ
cast.who: The incarnate Son, whose manhood is the way to the Father.

cast.name: the Father
cast.who: God the Father, whose nature is signified by truth and life.

cast.name: the Spirit
cast.who: The Spirit to whom the human Christ fittingly joins believers; the text does not specify 'Holy' Spirit, and the referent is ambiguous.

voices.speaker: Christ
voices.how_marked: Introduced by 'therefore Christ said' (Διὸ καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἔλεγεν) and quoted directly.

key_terms.sense: The way; in this work it signifies Christ's human, bodily, visible covering, a portion of earth and perceptible ground.
Truth; an intelligible reality that falls under neither sight nor touch, signifying the Father's nature.
Life; paired with truth as signifying the Father's nature.
The manhood or human nature of Christ, the starting point of the paths of righteousness.
The covering or garment; here the human, bodily, visible covering of Christ signified by 'way.'
Paradise, the destination to which the human Christ guides believers.
Pasture or dwelling place; the proper abode to which Christ restores believers.

scripture: The fragment quotes John 14:6. The author uses the Septuagint tradition; no Old Testament book names or Psalm numbering appear in this fragment.
uncertain: The exact date of composition is unknown.
The original addressee or audience is not stated in the fragment.
The precise extent of the original treatise cannot be determined from the surviving fragment.
Whether τῷ Πνεύματι refers to the Holy Spirit or the human spirit is ambiguous in the text.

_unresolved_facts.claim: This human Christ fittingly joins believers to the Spirit
_unresolved_facts.fix: The human Christ fittingly joins the Spirit to believers / fittingly adapts the Spirit to believers (the Greek προσαρμόττει τῷ Πνεύματι takes a dative of advantage, but the syntax is ambiguous: the Spirit is the object joined, or the means by which believers are joined; the subject 'man of Christ' acts upon the Spirit, not joining believers to the Spirit)

_unresolved_facts.claim: The Spirit to whom the human Christ fittingly joins believers
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Spirit whom the human Christ fittingly joins/adapts (the dative τῷ Πνεύματι is the object of προσαρμόττει, not the recipient of believers)

_unresolved_facts.claim: the human 'way' leads believers to the divine 'truth and life' of the Father
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὁ ἄνθρωπος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῖς κρείττοσι τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων προσάγων ἡμᾶς...Σεμνοπρεπῶς προσαρμόττει τῷ Πνεύματι, ξεναγεῖ εἰς τὸν παράδεισον, εἰς τὴν οἰκείαν ἀποκαθίστησι νομήν
_unresolved_facts.fix: the human 'way' leads believers to better pursuits, joins the Spirit, guides into paradise, and restores to proper pasture; the 'truth and life' signify the Father's nature but the text does not explicitly say the way 'leads to' truth and life as a destination

_unresolved_facts.claim: ὁ ἄνθρωπος τοῦ Χριστοῦ as a source form for 'Christ'
_unresolved_facts.fix: This source form should be listed under a separate entry for 'the man of Christ' or 'Christ's manhood/humanity', not under 'Christ'—it refers to Christ's human nature, not Christ simpliciter
